solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swimmer crossing river needs layer of protective cover

indicators.note: a fish crossing something lies astride it, so its letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: a tench is a freshwater fish
R is the standard abbreviation for river
a coat of paint is a layer

explanation.surface: A swimmer crossing a river needs an extra layer to keep warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the second half; the fish goes around the river to make the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trenchcoat is a belted waterproof overcoat, worn as a shield against rain and weather.

clue.text: Deliberate over time of trial

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: a set purpose is a deliberate, fixed one
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard about the date of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' reads as a verb, to ponder, but it is used as the adjective set; that word is turned over and time follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination or experiment, the same as a trial of quality or ability.

clue.text: Utter devastation of aunt and niece

indicators.note: devastation wrecks things, leaving the letters of the following words scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters of both relatives, the and being only a joiner

explanation.surface: Total ruin befalls two female relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning total, qualifying devastation, but it is the verb to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To enunciate is to pronounce words, so it is a synonym of utter as a verb of speech.

clue.text: It comes up during free consultation relating to one’s physical condition

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means rising from the bottom, so the word reads backwards
letters set free are released from their order and can be rearranged
during places one thing in the middle of another, so the first piece sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A topic arises in a free medical consultation about someone's health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' seems to mean no charge, but it signals the rearrangement of the next word, with the reversed word placed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Constitution means a person's bodily make-up, so the adjective describes anything bearing on their health.

clue.text: Come together for prayer

blocks.note: first meaning: to gather or assemble
second meaning, stressed on the first syllable: a short prayer in the liturgy

explanation.surface: A congregation gathers for worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are said differently: col-LECT for gathering, COL-lect for the short prayer of the day in Anglican and Catholic services.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds collect when they gather, and a collect is a brief set prayer read in church.

clue.text: Starts to attend lectures giving extra support in this branch of learning

indicators.note: the starts of the next few words are their opening letters, which are kept

blocks.note: the first letters of four words
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A student goes to lectures for extra help in their subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' sounds academic, like tutoring, but it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a field of mathematics, so it is a subject or discipline of study.

clue.text: Obscure rock band

blocks.note: first meaning: to make indistinct
second meaning: the Britpop group fronted by Damon Albarn

explanation.surface: A little-known group plays rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective, little-known, but it is the verb to smudge. Blur was a 1990s Britpop band.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to make it hazy or indistinct, hiding it from clear sight.

clue.text: Revolutionary passage from Bakunin eloquently sent up

indicators.note: a passage from a text is an extract, so the letters run on inside the following words
in a down clue, sent up means pushed upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A quotation from the anarchist Bakunin, eloquent in itself, gets mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Bakunin was a 19th-century Russian anarchist, which makes 'sent up' look like satire rather than a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolshevik seizure of power in Russia in 1917, a famous revolutionary.

clue.text: Rejects general opinion about help being withdrawn by son

indicators.note: something withdrawn is drawn back, so these letters run backwards
about means surrounding, so the opinion word goes around the help

blocks.note: repute is the general opinion people hold of someone
aid means help
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Public opinion turns against aid being cut off by a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By son' adds the abbreviation at the end, after the reversed help has been placed inside the reputation word.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to refuse to accept or disown, a close synonym of reject.

clue.text: Sailor extremely earnest in support of conventional means of restraint

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its outermost letters

blocks.note: straight means conventional or orthodox
Jack, or Jack tar, is a sailor
the two ends of the word

explanation.surface: A very serious sailor backs traditional methods of discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece 'in support of' another sits beneath it, so the sailor and the ends of earnest follow the conventional word.
explanation.definitionFit: A straitjacket is a garment with long sleeves tied behind, used to restrain a violent person.

clue.text: Turn down odds on return game with Norway

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the game's letters are read backwards

blocks.note: SP is the starting price, a bookmaker's odds
RU is rugby union
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A gambler declines the betting odds on a return match against Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return game' sounds like a rematch; here it only reverses the rugby abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with contempt, so it means to refuse or turn down an offer.

clue.text: Not serious over acquiring space to relax

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the space ends up inside the other letters

blocks.note: light as in light reading, not weighty
an en is a printer's unit of space
time's up means time's over

explanation.surface: Someone flippant is getting more room to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words light and over join, and the printer's space goes between them. An en is half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is an informal phrase for becoming less tense or serious, that is, to chill out.

clue.text: Absent-minded bishop caught in exotic dancer’s attire

indicators.note: exotic means outlandish and strange, so the letters take on an unfamiliar new arrangement
something caught in something else is held inside it

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dozy cleric is spotted wearing an exotic dancer's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic dancer' reads as one phrase, but exotic is the signal and dancer's attire is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatterbrained describes someone disorganised and forgetful, who cannot keep their thoughts in order.

clue.text: Nurse dead quiet at first about getting wasted

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word just before
about means around and astray, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A nurse, dead quiet at first, is gossiped about for being drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like slang for drunk; it is the sense frittered away. 'Dead quiet' seems a single phrase, but dead joins the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Squandered means spent recklessly, so money or chances squandered have been wasted.

clue.text: Not quite three months to the opening of this film

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped
an opening is the very start, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: a quarter of a year is three months
the first letter

explanation.surface: A film is under three months away from its premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as a premiere; it only picks the first letter of 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartet is a 2012 comedy-drama directed by Dustin Hoffman, set in a retirement home for musicians.

clue.text: City impressive after Aguero’s debut? Just the opposite

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is the one kept
this reverses the stated order, so the impressive word comes first and the other piece follows

blocks.note: august means grand and majestic
the first letter

explanation.surface: Manchester City look impressive after Agüero's first appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Sergio Agüero was Manchester City's star striker, so 'City' feels like the football club; it is the definition. Read literally the clue puts the A first; the tag reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is the state capital of Maine, and also a city in Georgia known for its golf course.

clue.text: Support for China’s not affected

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: China's backing is unaffected by recent events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not affected' reads as unchanged, but not is part of the material and affected is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar that props up a structure, a physical prop.

clue.text: Turned away from Green Party leader following piece of advice

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter
vert is the heraldic word for green
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this was set

explanation.surface: Someone ignores the Green Party leader after a word of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Party leader' reads as one title, but it splits into the colour and a leader's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Averted means directed elsewhere, as when eyes are averted, so it means turned away.

clue.text: Stop working without overall in eating area

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: an engine dies when it stops working
nett means overall, after all deductions

explanation.surface: A worker downs tools because they have no overall to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' looks like the work garment, but it is the adjective, total.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining space, usually an alcove off a kitchen, where meals are taken.

clue.text: Quote said to contain bit of uneasiness about volunteers is put in context

indicators.note: said tells us to take the spoken form of the word, spelt another way
a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its first letter
about means turned round, so the volunteers' letters face the other way
to contain is to hold within, so the sounded word goes around the rest

blocks.note: to cite is to quote; the word sounds like a site
the first letter
the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A spoken quotation hints at some unease about volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: The sounded word is split after its third letter to take the first letter of uneasiness and the reversed volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: To situate something is to place it in a particular setting or position, so to set it in context.

clue.text: Becomes angry with witnesses getting embarrassed

blocks.note: to witness is to see; the verb in the third person
red in the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper when witnesses turn up and blush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witnesses' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for flaring into sudden fury, like a bull at a cape.

clue.text: Refuse to approve of unsanctioned dancing at church

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The vicar frowns on unauthorised dancing at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsanctioned' is itself a near-synonym of the answer's sense, but here it is purely material.
explanation.definitionFit: To discountenance is to show disfavour toward something, so to withhold approval of it.

clue.text: Wrong to maintain it’s a form of protest

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the first word holds the next one inside

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims a wrongful act is really just a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for is, linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a demonstration where protesters occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Somalia oddly sent back charitable donations

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the odd positions: first, third, fifth, seventh
sent back means returned the way it came, so the kept letters read backwards

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: Aid to Somalia is strangely returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like strangely, but it selects the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are money or food given to the poor, a traditional word for charity.

clue.text: Muscle in president’s back almost damaged by overstretching

indicators.note: back means read in the backward direction, so the president's name runs right to left
almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: Jimmy Carter was US president 1977 to 1981
a torn muscle is one damaged by overstretching

explanation.surface: A muscle in the president's back has been strained from overstretching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President's back' reads as his spine; it is the name of a president turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is an anatomical muscle that draws a body part back or inward.

clue.text: Rule introduced to do away with whale food

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put inside it

blocks.note: R is an abbreviation for rule
to do away with is to kill

explanation.surface: A regulation is brought in to abolish whale feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do away with' reads as abolish, but it is the darker sense, murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny shrimp-like crustaceans that baleen whales filter from the sea in vast numbers.

clue.text: Robbed when working in the centre of Bordeaux

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, here its two central letters
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
the middle two of eight letters

explanation.surface: A traveller is mugged while on business in Bordeaux.
explanation.walkthrough: Done is British slang for cheated or swindled, as in 'I've been done'.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage, to be done is to be cheated or swindled out of money.

clue.text: He notices many filled with earth as they’re put up at the end of the road

definitions.text: they’re put up at the end of the road

indicators.note: something filled with another thing has it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
ads are advertisements, public notices
tons means a great many
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: A man spots lots of signs filled with soil being erected at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the road is life's road, and memorials mark its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravestones are erected over graves, marking the end of the journey through life.
